title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has two parts.

(1) It closes the computation from the previous page. There I is a finite poset indexing strata, and each flag (chain) d in I has an associated 'unfolded' space Σ_d. For an initial segment d=(i_1,…,i_p) of d'=(i_1,…,i_n), the fibration Σ_{d'}→Σ_d has fibres that are manifolds with boundary. The boundary is stratified by the Σ_{d''} with d''=d∐d''_0, where d''_0 strictly contains d'_0=(i_{p+1},…,i_n) and d'_0 is cofinal in d''_0. These d''_0 correspond bijectively to flags in I_{i_p<·<i_{p+1}} ∐ … ∐ I_{i_{n-1}<·<i_n}.

The conclusion on this page reads (with corrected transcription): Σ_{d'}→Σ_d is smooth, i.e. a fibration with boundaryless fibres, in all cases if and only if the sequence i_p,i_{p+1},…,i_n is saturated. Grothendieck stresses the sequence starts at i_p, not at i_1. Saturated means each term after the first is an immediate successor in I of the previous one. This is the multi-step version of the earlier statement: Σ_j→Σ_i is smooth iff j is a successor of i.

(2) §11, 'Digression': the index poset I is replaced by a topological ordered set. Σ=(Σ(0),Σ(1)) consists of:
- a space Σ(0);
- a closed subset Σ(1)⊂Σ(0)×Σ(0) that is the graph of an order.

Two hypotheses are imposed:
- (a) the target map Σ(1)→Σ(0), (i,j)↦j, is a 'locally bounding' immersion (locally like the inclusion of boundary faces), proper with finite fibres. So each j has only finitely many predecessors, and these vary locally like boundary sheets.
- (b) the diagonal Σ(0)→Σ(1) is an isomorphism onto an open and closed part. Its complement Σ*(1) = {(i,j): i<j} is therefore also open and closed.

Σ*(n) is the space of strict chains i_0<…<i_n. Together these form a semi-simplicial space ('pré-semi-simplicial'), i.e. the strict nerve with face maps only. Grothendieck remarks that degeneracies live in the full nerve Σ(n).

Purpose: generalise the dévissage/déploiement of stratified spaces, where strata are indexed by a discrete poset, to a setting where the index object is itself a space. The natural motivating case is self-intersecting strata or boundary faces. There the face map is only an immersion, not an embedding (normal crossings with non-normal components; manifolds with corners whose faces are not embedded). The next page goes on with cocartesian squares of flags and the corresponding Σ' diagrams, and with families of maps that must be 'bordantes'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The saturation criterion is consistent with the previous page: the boundary-stratifying set Drap(∐ intervals) is empty iff every open interval (i_k,i_{k+1}) is empty.

In (a), 'immersion' must be meant in the corner/boundary sense (local homeomorphism onto boundary sheets), since on the open-closed diagonal part the target map is the identity. The notion 'localement bordante' is not defined on this page.
§11 breaks off before any result is stated, so it is unfinished.

ideas.what: Σ_{d'}→Σ_d is smooth iff the tail chain i_p<…<i_n is saturated (consecutive immediate successors) in I.
ideas.modern_name: Smoothness of face/corner fibrations in the unzipping of a stratified space; saturated chains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on resolving Whitney stratified spaces into manifolds with corners (Mather/Thom control data; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzipping', 2017)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of a 'dévissage' of stratified structures is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6

ideas.what: Index poset of strata replaced by a topological poset with closed order graph, target map a proper, finite, 'locally bounding' immersion, and diagonal open-closed.
ideas.modern_name: Topological/étale poset (ordered topological space à la Nachbin) as indexing object for strata or faces; cf. the boundary immersion ∂X→X in Joyce's manifolds with corners; generalized cone complexes with self-gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nachbin (ordered spaces, 1965); Joyce (manifolds with corners, 2009–2012); Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (generalized cone complexes, 2015)

ideas.what: Strict nerve Σ*(n) of chains i_0<…<i_n as a semi-simplicial space, with degeneracies only in the full nerve Σ(n).
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) nerve of a topological poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts to extend the déploiement (unfolding) of stratified spaces to strata indexed by a topological poset whose face/target map is only a locally bounding immersion. This would cover self-intersecting strata, where the poset of strata is not a well-defined discrete object. The digression stops after setting up the hypotheses.
missed.quote: Σ(1) --but--> Σ(0) est une immersion localement bordante, et propre (à fibres finies)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Conically smooth / exit-path theories (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) usually fix a discrete poset of strata. An unfolding theory with an étale or topological index object is what is needed for normal-crossings with self-intersections and for log/tropical skeleta with self-glued faces.

missed.claim: Hypothesis (a) anticipates the modern treatment of manifolds with corners in which the boundary map ∂X→X is a proper immersion with finite fibres, not an embedding (Joyce). It also anticipates generalized cone complexes, whose face structure is a topological/étale poset with a semi-simplicial strict nerve. Grothendieck ties this directly to the déploiement of stratified spaces.
missed.quote: Σ*(n) l'espace des chaînes strictes i_0<i_1<…<i_n … un espace pré-semi-simplicial (NB pas d'opérations de dégénérescence …)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests a common framework: an 'étale poset of faces' unifying Joyce-style corners, the AFT unzipping of stratified spaces, and tropical/log cone complexes. To my knowledge this unification is not made explicitly in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The saturation criterion is routine. The topologised index-poset digression is a genuinely forward-looking formalism matching later corner and cone-complex theories, but it is only a setup with no results.

The word read as 'structure' is probably 'saturée'.
Section title is probably 'Digression : cas où I est topologique' (or 'cas d'un I topologique'), not 'catégorie'.
'Soit donné un ensemble ordonné topologique, i.e. un ensemble ordonné [objet] Σ = Σ(0), Σ(1)': the crossed-out words are 'espace topologique'.
In (b), 'une immersion [?] sur une partie ouverte et fermée' should read 'un isomorphisme sur une partie ouverte et fermée'.
